topic.subject: science
topic.title: Motion
topic.scope: distance vs displacement, speed vs velocity, acceleration, uniform circular motion, graphs, equations of motion

nodes.name: Speed is distance per unit time
Velocity is displacement per unit time
Acceleration is change in velocity over time
Slope of d-t graph is speed
Slope of v-t graph is acceleration
Area under v-t graph is displacement

misconceptions.statement: Displacement and distance are always the same value.
misconceptions.why: Students ignore the path taken and only look at the total length covered in everyday contexts.
misconceptions.fix: Distance is the total path length, while displacement is only the straight-line distance between the start and end points.

probe.question: An athlete runs one full lap of a 400m circular track. What is their displacement?

misconceptions.root_belief: a word means its everyday meaning

misconceptions.statement: Displacement cannot be zero if an object has moved.
misconceptions.why: In everyday language, 'displaced' means something was moved from its original spot and stayed elsewhere.
misconceptions.fix: If the initial and final positions are the same, the displacement is zero regardless of the distance traveled.

probe.question: You go to school and come back home. What is your net displacement?
probe.wrong_answer: The distance from home to school and back.

misconceptions.root_belief: what you cannot see does not exist

misconceptions.statement: Velocity is just another word for speed.
misconceptions.why: In common conversation, speed and velocity are used interchangeably.
misconceptions.fix: Velocity is speed with a specific direction; it changes if either the speed or the direction changes.

probe.question: A car travels at 50 km/h North and another at 50 km/h South. Do they have the same velocity?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, because both are going at 50 km/h.

misconceptions.root_belief: a word means its everyday meaning

misconceptions.statement: If an object's speed is constant, its velocity must be constant.
misconceptions.why: Students focus on the numerical value (magnitude) and ignore the directional component of velocity.
misconceptions.fix: Velocity changes if the direction of motion changes, even if the speed remains the same.

probe.question: A car turns a corner at a constant speed of 20 km/h. Is its velocity constant?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, because the speed is not changing.

misconceptions.root_belief: one property defines the whole concept

misconceptions.statement: Acceleration only means an object is speeding up.
misconceptions.why: The word 'accelerate' in cars and daily life specifically refers to increasing speed.
misconceptions.fix: Acceleration is any change in velocity, which includes speeding up, slowing down, or changing direction.

probe.question: A car applies brakes to slow down. Is it accelerating?
probe.wrong_answer: No, it is decelerating, which is not acceleration.

misconceptions.root_belief: a word means its everyday meaning

misconceptions.statement: Zero acceleration means the object is not moving.
misconceptions.why: Students confuse the rate of change of motion with the motion itself.
misconceptions.fix: Zero acceleration means the velocity is constant; the object could be moving at a very high speed.

probe.question: A spaceship moves in deep space at 10,000 km/h with its engines off. What is its acceleration?

misconceptions.root_belief: one event has one single cause

misconceptions.statement: Negative acceleration always means the object is moving backwards.
misconceptions.why: Students associate the negative sign with the direction of the velocity rather than the change in velocity.
misconceptions.fix: Negative acceleration means the acceleration vector points in the opposite direction of the chosen positive axis; it often means slowing down.

probe.question: If a car moving East (positive) slows down, what is the sign of its acceleration?
probe.wrong_answer: Positive, because it is still moving East.

misconceptions.root_belief: a rule from whole numbers works everywhere

misconceptions.statement: A distance-time graph shows the actual physical path of the object.
misconceptions.why: Students interpret the shape of the line as a map of the road or track.
misconceptions.fix: The graph shows how distance changes over time, not the spatial direction of the movement.

probe.question: A distance-time graph shows a hill shape. Does this mean the object went up a hill?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, the object moved upwards and then downwards.

misconceptions.root_belief: what you see is what it is

misconceptions.statement: A horizontal line on a velocity-time graph means the object is at rest.
misconceptions.why: Students carry over the rule from distance-time graphs where a flat line means no movement.
misconceptions.fix: A horizontal line on a v-t graph means the velocity is constant and not zero.

probe.question: A v-t graph shows a straight horizontal line at v = 5 m/s. Is the object moving?

misconceptions.root_belief: a rule from one context works everywhere

misconceptions.statement: The equations of motion can be used for any moving object.
misconceptions.why: Students apply formulas without checking the underlying assumptions or constraints.
misconceptions.fix: The three equations of motion (v=u+at, etc.) only apply when acceleration is uniform (constant).

probe.question: Can we use s = ut + 1/2 at^2 for a car whose acceleration is changing every second?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, as long as we know the average acceleration.

misconceptions.root_belief: a rule from one context works everywhere

misconceptions.statement: An object in uniform circular motion has zero acceleration because its speed is constant.
misconceptions.why: Students believe acceleration only exists if the speedometer reading changes.
misconceptions.fix: In circular motion, the direction changes constantly, which means the velocity changes, so there is acceleration.

probe.question: A stone is whirled in a circle at a constant speed of 2 m/s. Is it accelerating?
probe.wrong_answer: No, because the speed is not increasing or decreasing.

misconceptions.root_belief: one property defines the whole concept

misconceptions.statement: The area under a graph is always measured in square meters (area units).
misconceptions.why: Students confuse the geometric calculation of area with the physical quantity it represents.
misconceptions.fix: The area under a graph represents the product of the quantities on the x and y axes; for a v-t graph, this is displacement (meters).

probe.question: What does the area under a velocity (m/s) vs time (s) graph represent?
probe.wrong_answer: The surface area of the path.

misconceptions.root_belief: a word means its everyday meaning
